title: PEPFAR Extension Act of 2018
official_summary:
PEPFAR Extension Act of 2018

This bill amends the United States Leadership Against HIV/AIDS, Tuberculosis, and Malaria Act of 2003 to extend certain provisions related to the U.S. President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR), a government initiative addressing the global HIV/AIDS epidemic. Specifically, the bill extends through FY2023 provisions that:

  • require the Inspectors General of the Department of State and the U.S. Agency for Global Media, jointly with the Department of Health and Human Services and the U.S. Agency for International Development, to coordinate and conduct oversight of PEPFAR programs,
  • limit U.S. contributions to the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria to 33% of funds contributed from all sources,
  • require that certain fund contributions be withheld under specified circumstances, such as if funds were previously used to assist a country that has repeatedly supported acts of international terrorism, and
  • require that more than half of the PEPFAR budget be allocated for specified HIV/AIDS treatment and care.

The bill also extends through FY2024 annual reporting requirements relating to HIV/AIDS treatment providers and costs.

summary.headline: This law extends several PEPFAR oversight, funding-limit, and reporting rules for global HIV/AIDS programs through 2023 and 2024.
summary.what_it_does: The law changes the 2003 act that created PEPFAR, the U.S. global HIV/AIDS program. It extends oversight duties for inspectors general across several federal agencies through fiscal year 2023. It keeps a cap that limits U.S. money to the Global Fund to 33 percent of total contributions, and it keeps rules requiring some funds to be withheld in certain cases, such as when aid went to a country that repeatedly supported terrorism. It also extends a rule that more than half of the PEPFAR budget go to HIV/AIDS treatment and care, and extends yearly reports on treatment providers and costs through fiscal year 2024.

who_it_affects.group: People receiving HIV/AIDS treatment and care in countries supported by PEPFAR
who_it_affects.how: The rules keep a set share of the program's budget directed toward treatment and care services.

who_it_affects.group: Health care providers and organizations that deliver HIV/AIDS treatment abroad
who_it_affects.how: They are covered by annual federal reporting requirements on treatment providers and costs, which are extended through fiscal year 2024.

who_it_affects.group: Federal inspectors general at the State Department, U.S. Agency for Global Media, HHS, and USAID
who_it_affects.how: They must continue coordinating and conducting joint oversight of PEPFAR programs through fiscal year 2023.

who_it_affects.group: The Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria
who_it_affects.how: U.S. contributions are capped at 33 percent of total funds from all sources, and some contributions may be withheld under set conditions.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 11, 2018; the extended provisions run through fiscal year 2023, and the reporting requirements through fiscal year 2024.
